title: Compliance Note on Small-Balance Cash-Outs and Purchase Refunds for Cartwise Gift Cards
content:
Two ways exist for value to leave a Cartwise Gift Cards card other than by paying for orders: a small-balance cash-out to the holder where state law requires it, and a purchase refund to the purchaser of an unredeemed card. The state list, the cash-out threshold and each card type's purchase refund window are those of the cash-out and refund schedule.

## Part A — Small-balance cash-out

A.1 A holder whose profile address is in one of the states on the cash-out list may cash out the card when its purchased balance is at or below the cash-out threshold.

A.2 Bonus value is not paid out: it is never cashed out, and it lapses.

A.3 Only the holder can request a cash-out. The cash-out is the holder's own act.

A.4 The cash-out closes the card: the card moves from active to closed, and the value paid out leaves the card as a removal for cash-out.

### Cash-out illustrations (hypothetical inputs, threshold 10.00)

| Holder's profile address | Purchased balance | Bonus value on the card | Outcome under Part A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oregon (on the list) | 10.00 | none | May cash out 10.00; the card closes |
| Oregon (on the list) | 10.01 | none | Above the threshold; Part A provides no cash-out |
| Washington (on the list) | 6.00 | 10.00 | May cash out 6.00; the 10.00 of bonus value is not paid and lapses; the card closes |

## Part B — Purchase refund

B.1 A purchaser may have an unredeemed card refunded within the purchase refund window counted from the purchase.

B.2 The purchase refund window is counted in calendar days with the card's purchase date as day 0, and the last day is the purchase date plus the card type's purchase refund window in days, inclusive.

B.3 A card with any redemption is not refundable, because every card type requires a refunded card never to have been redeemed.

B.4 A purchase refund removes the card's value as a removal for purchase refund.

B.5 The purchase date and the card's redemptions are read from the company's record of that card.

### Window boundary (hypothetical inputs)

For a card type with a 30-day window and a card purchased on 1 June:

| Date of the refund | Count from purchase | Within the window? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 June | day 0 | Yes |
| 1 July | day 30 (purchase date plus 30 days) | Yes — last day, inclusive |
| 2 July | day 31 | No |

For a card type with a 14-day window, day 14 is the last day on which the refund is within the window, and day 15 is outside it.

### Conditions combined

| Within the window | Card never redeemed | Purchase refund |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Available to the purchaser |
| Yes | No — any redemption | Not refundable |
| No | any | Not refundable |
